3.2.
G
-symmetric monoidality of localizing motives

We now come to the heart of the matter, and prove in this subsection the following, which is the main result of this paper.

Theorem 3.2.1
.

Let
w:W\to V
be a map of finite
G
-sets. The functor
f_{\otimes}:\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{W}\to\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}
sends motivic equivalences to motivic equivalences (cf.
3.1.4
).

Given this, it is then rather immediate to obtain the following:

Theorem 3.2.2
.

There exists a unique
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
compatible with the norm
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
under the localization
G
-functor
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
. Furthermore, for any
G
-symmetric monoidal
G
-presentable
G
-stable
G
-category
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
, restriction along
\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
induces a equivalences

\underline{{\func}}^{L,\otimes}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{fin.loc.},\otimes}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}),\hskip 9.24994pt\underline{{\func}}^{L,\otimes\mathrm{-lax}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{fin.loc.},\otimes\mathrm{-lax}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})

between the
G
-category of
G
-symmetric monoidal (resp.
G
-lax symmetric monoidal),
G
-colimit-preserving functors and the
G
-category of
G
-symmetric monoidal (resp.
G
-lax symmetric monoidal) finitary
G
-localizing invariants.

Proof.

The first statement follows immediately from
3.2.1
and
2.1.22
. The second statement for
G
-symmetric monoidal (resp.
G
-lax symmetric monoidal) functors is then a combination of
[
QS25
, Lem. 5.28 (3)]
with
3.1.13
.
∎

Before embarking on the proof proper, let us first give a sketch of the strategy thereof. Suppose we are given a motivic equivalence
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
in
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}
. Our task is to prove that
\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
is a motivic equivalence in
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
, i.e. we need to show that
\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
is an equivalence in
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
. By the isotropy separation from
2.2.7
using the family
\mathcal{P}
of proper subgroups of
G
and inducting on the size of the group, we are essentially reduced to proving that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
is an equivalence in
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
for the inductive step. We will in fact show that the functor
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
of nonequivariant categories is a Mackey
H
-localizing invariant.

In turn, by virtue of the behaviour of distributive functors with respect to cofiber sequences as in
2.1.19
, most of the work for this will go into proving (i) that, upon applying
\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}
to a
H
-Karoubi sequence, the first map from the cube in the lemma is fully faithful to verify that it is a
G
-Karoubi sequence; and (ii) that the functor
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}
erases the undesirable cubical colimits. We formulate these steps precisely in the following key proposition, for which we recall
2.1.20
for the filtration of equivariant cubes.

Proposition 3.2.3
.

Consider the map
f:G/H\to G/G
.
Suppose we have a Karoubi sequence
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
in
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}
. Then:

(1)

the induced functor

\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{f_{*}[1]\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\longrightarrow f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}

is fully faithful, with cofiber
f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
;

(2)

for every
1\leq i\leq|G/H|
, the map

\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{(f_{*}[1])_{\leq i-1}\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\longrightarrow\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{(f_{*}[1])_{\leq i}\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})

is fully faithful with cofiber given by a finite sum of properly induced categories.

Together, these claims imply that
modulo motives of properly induced categories
,

f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\to f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\to f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}

is a motivic cofiber sequence, thus proving that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}=\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}f_{\otimes}
is a localizing invariant (its finitariness being automatic). In more precise terms, we obtain:

Corollary 3.2.4
.

Let
f\colon W\rightarrow V
be a map between orbits in
\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
and
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
a Karoubi sequence in
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{W}
. Then
f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\rightarrow f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
is sent to a cofiber sequence in
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{\mathrm{Mot}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
. In particular,
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}f_{\otimes}(-):\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{W}\to\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
is a finitary Mackey
W
-localizing invariant.

Proof.

By
3.2.3
(1), we get a Karoubi sequence

\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{f_{*}[1]\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\longrightarrow f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\longrightarrow f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}

and hence, an equivalence in
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}

\frac{\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})}{\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{f_{*}[1]\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))}\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}).

We claim now that the map

(6)

\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{(f_{\otimes}[1])_{\leq i-1}\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\longrightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{(f_{\otimes}[1])_{\leq i}\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))

is an equivalence for all
1\leq i\leq|G/H|
. Given this, we thus see that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{f_{*}[1]\setminus 1}f_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))
is an equivalence, so that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})/\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
is indeed an equivalence in
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
, hence proving that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}f_{\otimes}
is a Mackey
G
-localizing invariant – that it is finitary is immediate from
f_{\otimes}
preserving filtered colimits by
2.1.17
, and that the functors
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}
and
\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
do too.

To prove the claim we note that since
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
is a
V
-localizing invariant,
3.2.3
(2) implies that the cofiber of
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}
applied to
Equation

6
is
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
applied to a properly induced object, and therefore is
0
. This completes the proof.
∎

Let us now work towards proving
3.2.3
. The main tool for this will be the isotropy separation criterion
2.3.1
to check fully faithfulness of functors. As such, the proof will be inductive and we first establish it in the nonequivariant base case when
G=e
. This will use the following abstract categorical lemma.

Lemma 3.2.5
.

Let
I
be a poset with binary joins, and let
F:I^{\triangleright}\to\mathrm{Pr}^{L}
be a cocone such that for each
i\in I,F(i)\to F(\infty)
is fully faithful and has a colimit-preserving right adjoint. If for each
i,j\in I
and
k\in I^{\triangleright},k\geq i,j
, the following square is vertically right adjointable:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(i\wedge j)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(j)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(k)}}

then the induced map
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F(i)\to F(\infty)
is fully faithful.

Note that the adjointability condition for a general
k\in I^{\triangleright}
follows from the case of
k=\infty
. Thus, the assumptions are slightly redundant.

Proof.

We will show that the following square is also vertically right adjointable:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(i\wedge j)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(j)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{F(i)}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F}}

Given this, we can argue as follows: let
L:\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F\to F(\infty)
denote the induced functor, and let
\iota_{i}:F(i)\to\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F
denote the inclusions and
f_{i}:F(i)\to F(\infty)
the maps induced by
F
. We prove that the unit
\mathrm{id}\to L^{R}L
is an equivalence. The images of
\iota_{i}:F(i)\to\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F,i\in I
jointly generate
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{I}F
under colimits, so it suffices to prove that
\iota_{j}^{R}\iota_{i}\to\iota_{j}^{R}L^{R}L\iota_{i}
is an equivalence for all
i,j\in I
. But
L\iota_{i}=f_{i}
by design, so this is the canonical map
\iota_{j}^{R}\iota_{i}\to f_{j}^{R}f_{i}
, which is an equivalence by adjointability of the two squares, since they are both equivalent to
F(i\wedge j\to j)\circ F(i\wedge j\to i)^{R}
(and we can check compatibility of the maps).

In turn, the adjointability of the square with the colimit follows from our adjointability assumption and the description of colimits in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}
as limits along the right adjoints: consider the transformation
F(i\wedge-)\to F
of functors
I\rightarrow\mathrm{Pr}^{L}
and the induced map on colimits
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{j\in I}F(i\wedge j)\to\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{j\in I}F(j)
. By adjointability, we may view this map between colimits as a map
\lim_{j\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(i\wedge j)\to\lim_{j\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(j)
in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}
which is again given levelwise by
F(i\wedge j)\to F(j)
, natural in
j\in I^{\mathrm{op}}
. In particular, this naturality gives us the outer commuting diagrams

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(i)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lim_{j\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(i\wedge j)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lim_{j\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(j)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(i\wedge j)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F(j)}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

which were the squares sought after.
∎

Using this, we can now prove the nonequivariant base case, which is a stable analogue of
[
HRS25
, Cor. 5.9]
:

Proposition 3.2.6
.

Let
n\geq 1
be an integer, and consider a family
f_{i}:\mathcal{A}_{i}\to\mathcal{B}_{i}
of fully faithful exact functors between stable categories. Consider the induced cube

C_{f}:[1]^{n}\xrightarrow{(f_{i})_{i}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{\times n}\xrightarrow{\bigotimes_{n}}\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}},

and for
i\leq n
, let
[1]^{n}_{\leq i}\subset[1]^{n}
denote the full subposet spanned by sequences with a number of
1
’s smaller or equal to
i
.

For all
i\leq n-1
, the map
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i}}C_{f}\to\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i+1}}C_{f}
is fully faithful. In particular, for
i=n-1
, the map
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}\setminus\{1\}}C_{f}\to\bigotimes_{j}\mathcal{B}_{j}
is fully faithful.

Proof.

Since fully faithfulness may also be checked after taking Ind-completions, we consider the composite
C_{f}\colon[1]^{n}\rightarrow\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ind}}\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
landing in presentable categories, where the functor
\mathrm{Ind}
is symmetric monoidal. Note that the value of
C_{f}
at a morphism
S\rightarrow T
in
[1]^{n}
, i.e. an inclusion of subsets of
\underline{{n}}=\{1,\ldots,n\}
, is given by
\bigotimes_{\overline{s}\in\underline{{n}}\backslash S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}_{\overline{s}}\otimes\bigotimes_{s\in S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{s}\rightarrow\bigotimes_{\overline{t}\in\underline{{n}}\backslash T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}_{\overline{t}}\otimes\bigotimes_{t\in T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{t}
. Since
\mathrm{Ind}
preserves fully faithful functors and sends exact functors between stable categories to morphisms in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}
with colimit-preserving right adjoints, we see that
C_{f}\colon[1]^{n}\rightarrow\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
lands in fully faithful functors which admit colimit-preserving right adjoints. Furthermore, for
S,T\subseteq\underline{{n}}
, we claim that the square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{\overline{j}\in\underline{{n}}\backslash(S\cap T)}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}_{\overline{j}}\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in S\cap T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{j}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{\overline{t}\in\underline{{n}}\backslash T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}_{\overline{t}}\otimes\bigotimes_{t\in T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{t}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{\overline{s}\in\underline{{n}}\backslash S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}_{\overline{s}}\otimes\bigotimes_{s\in S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{s}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{i\in\underline{{n}}}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{i}}

is vertically right adjointable. To see this, observe that this square is obtained by tensoring the two morphisms

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{S\backslash T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{(S\cup T)^{c}}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}\otimes\bigotimes_{T\backslash S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}\otimes\bigotimes_{S\cap T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{(S\cup T)^{c}}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A}\otimes\bigotimes_{T\backslash S}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}\otimes\bigotimes_{S\cap T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bigotimes_{S\backslash T}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}}

where both (and in particular, the vertical) morphisms have colimit-preserving right adjoints. Since the tensor product in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
preserves internal adjunctions, the vertically right adjointed square is simply obtained by tensoring the horizontal morphism above with the right adjoint of the vertical morphism, and so the adjointed square commutes.

Therefore, by setting
I=[1]^{n}_{\leq i}
in
3.2.5
for
i\leq n-1
, we see that
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i}}C_{f}\rightarrow\bigotimes_{j}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{j}
is fully faithful for all
i\leq n-1
. Consequently also, by considering the composites
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i}}C_{f}\rightarrow\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i+1}}C_{f}\rightarrow\bigotimes_{j}\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B}_{j}
, we see also that the maps
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i}}C_{f}\rightarrow\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{[1]^{n}_{\leq i+1}}C_{f}
are fully faithful for
i\leq n-1
. This completes the proof.
∎

We are now ready for the proof of the proposition.

Proof of
3.2.3
.

The fully faithfulness in each statement will be done by induction on the order of
G
and we prove each in turn. To see (1), the statement about the cofiber is immediate from
2.1.19
. We will prove fully faithfulness by a stratification induction via
2.3.1
. The base case of
G=e
is known by
3.2.6
. We use the family of proper subgroups to apply
2.3.1
. By induction, we know the statement to be true upon restriction to all proper subgroups of
G
.

To wit, let
w\colon W\rightarrow V
and
u\colon U\rightarrow V
be morphisms in
\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
, where
u
is not an equivalence. And let
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
be an arbitrary
G
-cocomplete
G
-symmetric monoidal category (which we will later specialise to the case of
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
). Let
F\colon x\rightarrow y
be a morphism in
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}(W)
and consider the pullback
Z=W\times_{V}U
in
\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
as in
2.1.8
with
\overline{w}\colon Z\to U
,
\overline{u}\colon Z\to W
. Then
u^{*}
applied to
\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{w_{*}[1]-1}w_{\otimes}(x\rightarrow y)\rightarrow w_{\otimes}y
in
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}(V)
yields the analogous morphism

\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{\overline{w}_{*}[1]-1}\overline{w}_{\otimes}(\overline{u}^{*}x\rightarrow\overline{u}^{*}y)\longrightarrow\overline{w}_{\otimes}\overline{u}^{*}y.

Specialising to the case
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}=\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
,
x=\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
, and
y=\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
, this shows the statement upon restriction to proper subgroups by the inductive hypothesis.

Next, to see the statement on geometric fixed points, note by
[
HKK24
, Obs. 4.2.2]
that applying
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}
to the map of interest yields the map

\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}=\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{(w_{*}[1]-1)^{G}}\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}w_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\longrightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}.

By
2.3.2
,
w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightarrow w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
is fully faithful. By
2.3.1
, we know that
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}
preserves fully faithfulness, whence the desired statement. This completes the proof of (1).

Point (2) may be proved by a similar isotropy separation inductive proof using instead as an input
2.1.21
, where this time applying
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}
yields the map
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\longrightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
which is of course an equivalence.
∎

Armed with the requisite preparations, we finally come to the proof of the theorem.

Proof of
3.2.1
.

Since motivic equivalences in
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}
are exactly the preimage under
\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}
of equivalences, we may instead prove that
\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}-)
inverts motivic equivalences (be warned that it is however
not
a localizing invariant!).

Reduction to orbits:
We observe as a general claim that if
w_{i}\colon W_{i}\to V
satisfy this conclusion for
i
in some finite set
I
, then so does
\coprod_{i}w_{i}\colon\coprod_{i}W_{i}\to V
. Indeed, in this case
(\coprod_{i}w_{i})_{\otimes}\simeq\bigotimes_{i}(w_{i})_{\otimes}
, so it suffices to show that ordinary tensor products preserve motivic equivalences. The proof of this fact is the same as in
[
BGT14
, Lem. 5.5, Thm. 5.8]
(see also
[
RSW25
, Prop. 4.2]
) and simply follows from the fact that for any
V
-stable
V
-category
{\mathcal{C}}
,
{\mathcal{C}}\otimes-\colon\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}\to\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}
preserves Karoubi sequences. Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume
V
is an orbit, and we work by descending induction on the size of
V
(i.e. by induction on the size of stabilizers in
V
).

Induction hypothesis:
We assume the result holds for every map
w\colon W\to V^{\prime}
where
V^{\prime}
is a strictly larger orbit than
V
(i.e. strictly smaller isotropy subgroup), and we prove it for our given map
w\colon W\to V
. We may then write
W
as a coproduct of orbits, and by reducing to orbits as above, we may also assume that
W
is an orbit. We now argue by isotropy separation:

Geometric fixed points:
By
3.2.4
,
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}-)
is a finitary Mackey
W
-localizing invariant, and so it sends Mackey motivic equivalences to equivalences. By
3.1.12
, it therefore sends motivic equivalences to motivic equivalences. Thus it suffices to prove that for every proper orbit map
u\colon U\to V
,
u^{*}\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}-)
inverts motivic equivalences.

Proper subgroups:

Letting
Z
denote the pullback
W\times_{V}U
, with
\overline{w}\colon Z\to U
and
\overline{u}\colon Z\to W
as in
2.1.8
, we find
u^{*}\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{V}(f_{\otimes}-)\simeq\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{U}(u^{*}f_{\otimes}-)\simeq\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{U}(\overline{w}_{\otimes}\overline{u}^{*}-)
. Now
U\to V
is proper and hence
U
is a strictly larger orbit, so by induction,
\mathcal{U}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{U}(\overline{w}_{\otimes}-)
inverts motivic equivalences and since
\overline{u}^{*}
preserves motivic equivalences, we are done.
∎

Remark 3.2.7
.

The presentably symmetric monoidal category
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
has played only an auxiliary role in the story so far, but we think that it is a category that deserves further attention in matters pertaining to isotropy separation methods for equivariant algebraic K-theory. For example, by the universal property of the map
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
from
2.2.6
, we immediately get from
3.1.13
that

(\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G})^{*}\colon\underline{{\func}}^{L}(\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{fin.loc.}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})

for all
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
in the image of the inclusion
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}\subseteq\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
, i.e.
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
is the receptacle of the universal finitary
G
-localizing invariant which vanishes on properly induced categories.

While it might appear totally uncontrollable, observe nonetheless, for example, that
3.2.2
implies that it has
another
structure of a
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}
–commutative algebra in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
apart from the one coming from the universal property of
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}
as in
3.3.2
. To wit, the multiplicative norm yields the symmetric monoidal functor

(7)

\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}\xlongrightarrow{\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}}\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\xlongrightarrow{\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}}\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}.

This preserves all colimits by applying
3.2.4
in the case of
f\colon G/e\rightarrow G/G
, the universal property of
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}
, and that
\underline{{{\mathcal{U}}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
commutes with the norms by
3.2.2
.

By
3.3.6
below, the tensor unit of
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
corepresents
\Phi^{G}K_{G}(-)
, and so the map
Equation

7
may be viewed as a categorification of the map
K((-)^{e})\rightarrow\Phi^{G}K_{G}(-)
of functors
\mathrm{CAlg}_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp})
coming from applying
\Phi^{G}
to
\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}\res^{G}_{e}K_{G}(-)\rightarrow K_{G}(-)
and recalling that
\Phi^{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}\simeq\mathrm{id}
.

3.3.
Corepresentedness of localizing equivariant K–theory

We start by recording the equivariant analogue of
[
BGT13
, Prop. 9.26]
, namely corepresentability of equivariant
K
-theory in
G
-motives, specifically by the symmetric monoidal unit. Since
3.2.2
provides
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
with a
G
-symmetric monoidal structure, this will canonically endow

-theory with a

-lax symmetric monoidal structure.

.

which implies that the mapping

\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\colon\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\rightarrow\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}

∎

4.
Applications

4.1.
Borel localizing motives and tensor powers

Definition 4.1.1
.

A functor
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})\rightarrow\mathcal{E}
to a stable category
\mathcal{E}
is a
Borel
G
-localizing invariant
if it is additive and it sends Karoubi sequences to bifiber sequences. It is furthermore said to be
finitary
if it preserves filtered colimits. A morphism in
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
is said to be a
Borel motivic equivalence
if it is sent to an equivalence by all finitary Borel
G
-localizing invariants out of
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
.

Observation 4.1.2
.

The Borelification functor
b^{*}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\rightarrow\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
sends Mackey motivic equivalences to Borel motivic equivalences since it clearly sends Karoubi sequences to Karoubi sequences and it preserves filtered colimits.

Observation 4.1.3
.

The functor
(-)_{hG}\colon\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})\rightarrow\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}
sends Karoubi sequences to Karoubi sequences and it preserves filtered colimits. To see this, since
(-)_{hG}
is a left adjoint, it of course preserves cofiber sequences and filtered colimits. To see that it additionally takes Verdier sequences to fiber sequences, let
\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{B}\rightarrow{\mathcal{C}}
be a Karoubi sequence. Since
\mathcal{A}_{hG}\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{hG}\rightarrow{\mathcal{C}}_{hG}
is still a cofiber sequence, we only have to show that the functor
\mathcal{A}_{hG}\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{hG}
is fully faithful. To see this, simply note that under the equivalence
\mathrm{Ind}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st},\omega}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0mu(-)^{\omega}
, the fact that the inclusion
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st},\omega}\subset\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
preserves colimits, and that
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
is
\infty
-semiadditive, that the map
\mathcal{A}_{hG}\rightarrow\mathcal{B}_{hG}
is identified with
((\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A})^{hG})^{\omega}\rightarrow((\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B})^{hG})^{\omega}
. And this functor is certainly fully faithful since
(\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{A})^{hG}\rightarrow(\mathrm{Ind}\mathcal{B})^{hG}
is so.

Proposition 4.1.4
.

Let
X\in\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
. The functor
(-)^{\otimes X}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightarrow\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
sends motivic equivalences to Borel motivic equivalences. Consequently, the endofunctor
((-)^{\otimes X})_{hG}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightarrow\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}
preserves motivic equivalences.

Proof.

Since
X
is a finite coproduct
\coprod_{i}G/H_{i}
of orbits, we know that
(-)^{\otimes X}\simeq\bigotimes_{i}(-)^{\otimes G/H_{i}}
. Hence, it suffices to deal with the case when
X=G/H
for some subgroup
H\leq G
. In this case, first note that there is a factorization

(-)^{\otimes G/H}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\xrightarrow{\const_{H}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BH}\xhookrightarrow{b_{!}}\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}}\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\xrightarrow{b^{*}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BG}.

This is because
[
Hil26
, Thm. 2.4.10 (2)]
ensures that the composite
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}}\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\xrightarrow{b^{*}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BG}
is equivalent to
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}\xrightarrow{b^{*}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BH}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{N}^{G}_{H}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BG}
, and
b^{*}b_{!}\simeq\mathrm{id}
.

Next, note that the constant functor
\const_{H}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightarrow\func(BH,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
sends motivic equivalences to Borel motivic equivalences since it sends Karoubi sequences to Karoubi sequences and it preserves filtered colimits. Similarly, since
b_{!}\colon(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BH}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{H}\subset\mackey_{H}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
is levelwise given by taking the appropriate homotopy orbits,
b_{!}
sends Borel motivic equivalences to Mackey motivic equivalences by
4.1.3
. Moreover, by
4.1.2
,
b^{*}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\rightarrow(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BG}
sends Mackey motivic equivalences to Borel motivic equivalences. Hence, together with
3.2.1
, we learn that
(-)^{\otimes G/H}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightarrow(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{BG}
sends motivic equivalences to Borel motivic equivalences, as required.

The last statement about
((-)^{\otimes X})_{hG}
preserving motivic equivalences is now an immediate combination of the first statement together with the fact that
(-)_{hG}\colon\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})\rightarrow\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}
sends Borel motivic equivalences to motivic equivalences since
(-)_{hG}
preserves Karoubi sequences by
4.1.3
.
∎

Warning 4.1.5
.

While it was true that
(-)^{\otimes X}
and
((-)^{\otimes X})_{hG}
preserved the appropriate notions of motivic equivalences, it is
not
true that
((-)^{\otimes X})^{hG}
does since
(-)^{hG}
does not preserve Karoubi sequences, or filtered colimits. On the other hand, Efimov shows in
[
Efi25
, Cor. 3.30]
that this can be remedied by considering instead
dualizable
fixed points. Since
BG
is countable, we find that in conjunction with
[
Efi25a
, Thm. 4.26]
,
((-)^{X})^{hG,\mathrm{dual}}
does preserve motivic equivalences.

While this will not strictly be needed in the paper, we nevertheless clarify the relationship between the genuine equivariant localizing motives
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
that we have been considering so far with the notion of
Borel
localizing motives, i.e. the category
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
defined as the Dwyer-Kan localization of
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
against the Borel motivic equivalences.

Proposition 4.1.6
.

The category
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
is a Dwyer–Kan localization of
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
, and this localization fits into a commuting square of Dwyer–Kan localizations

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}.}

Proof.

The existence of the square is clear by the universal property of
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
and the fact that
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\rightarrow\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
preserves Karoubi sequences and filtered colimits. The fact that the morphism
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\rightarrow\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
is a Dwyer–Kan localization is now also clear, since the functor
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\to\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
is.
∎

Remark 4.1.7
.

Another perspective here, coming from
B.0.1
, is that while
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
can be described as the category of compactly generated modules over
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}
,
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
can be described as the category of compactly generated
\mathrm{Sp}^{BG}
-modules. The localization functor
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\to\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
can therefore be viewed as given by basechange along the Borelification functor
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}\to\mathrm{Sp}^{BG}
.

Warning 4.1.8
.

Be warned however that
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
is
not
the Borelification of
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}
. By the square from
4.1.6
and the fact that
\func(BG,\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})\rightarrow\func(BG,\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}})
is a Borel
G
-localizing invariant, the Bousfield localization
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{G}\rightarrow\func(BG,\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc}})

does
however factor uniquely through
\mathrm{Mot}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}_{G}
.

Remark 4.1.9
.

In fact, the square
4.1.6
can be assembled to a square of objects in
\mathrm{CAlg}_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}})
. Implicit in this claim is that
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}
admits the structure of multiplicative norms (which is a straightforward consequence of
4.1.4
). The remarks in the preceding warning then amounts to the statement that the map
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}}
induces an equivalence
\underline{{\mathrm{Bor}}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc}})\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{Bor}}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{bor}})
. We have chosen not to present this subsection as such since we would like to emphasize that our main theorem has consequences also in the unparametrized and nonequivariant setup.

4.2.
G
-symmetric monoidality of splitting motives

In this section, we explain how to
deduce
from our results the existence of a
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on the equivariant version of splitting motives.

Remark 4.2.1
.

It seems somewhat counterintuitive to prove a result about localizing motives and deduce one about splitting motives, since the latter are usually thought of as easier. However, the key technical input in our proof, namely
3.2.3
, seems harder to establish in the split case: one would have to prove that the relevant maps are not only fully faithful, but also have adjoints (upon assuming, of course, that the map
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\to\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
has the relevant adjoint). This is more tedious than establishing fully faithfulness. Therefore, while it is possible to give a direct proof, we opt for the path of least resistance and simply deduce the splitting results from the localizing results.

The basic idea for the deduction is that splitting motives (up to finitary-ness questions) are obtained from stable categories by inverting so-called “universal
K
-theory equivalences”, cf.
[
BGM+21
, Def. 4.4]
. Our construction of norms provides, inter alia, a map

N_{H}^{G}K_{H}(\underline{{\func}}_{H}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\to K_{G}(\underline{{\func}}_{G}^{\mathrm{ex}}(N_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},N_{H}^{G}\underline{{B}}))

compatible with compositions and natural in
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
. This will directly imply that
N_{H}^{G}
preserves universal
K
-theory equivalences, so that the general strategy from the end of the previous section will simply work here. So, all in all, the desired construction will be a direct corollary of the fact that the connective cover of nonconnective
K
-theory is connective
K
-theory.

We now give more details, starting with variants of splitting motives.

Definition 4.2.2
.

A
G
-splitting invariant
is a
G
-semiadditive
G
-functor
\underline{{E}}:\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\to\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
to some
G
-additive
G
-category
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
sending split Karoubi sequences to products - more precisely, so that for every split Karoubi sequence
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\rightleftharpoons\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\rightleftharpoons\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
, the induced map
\underline{{E}}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\to\underline{{E}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\times\underline{{E}}(\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}})
is an equivalence.

A
Mackey splitting invariant
is a functor
E:{\mathrm{Cat}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\to\mathcal{E}
to some additive category sending split Karoubi sequences to products.

A
universal
K_{G}
-theory
equivalence is a map in
{\mathrm{Cat}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
sent to an equivalence by any
G
-splitting invariant.

We have the obvious analogous definitions for finite
G
-sets
V
.

Remark 4.2.3
.

Note that the proof of
3.1.12
applies here too and so universal
K_{G}
-theory are equivalently those maps sent to an equivalence by any Mackey splitting invariant. The proof of
3.1.5
also applies and so universal
K_{G}
-theory equivalences are preserved by restriction functors.

We now define two
G
-categories of splitting motives, one of which is some kind of absolute variant with no finitary-ness or cocompleteness condition of Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada’s original definition of “additive motives”, and the other one is a variant which recovers an additive (as opposed to stable) variant of Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada’s original definition. There are many other variants, including stable variants (we only impose additivity), but the proof we give generalizes to these other variants quite easily.

Definition 4.2.4
.

The
G
-category of
absolute splitting
G
-motives

\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}
is the localization of the
G
-category
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
at the class of universal
K_{G}
-equivalences. The localization functor is denoted
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}
. The
G
-category of
finitary splitting
G
-motives

\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}
is defined as the sifted cocompletion
\underline{{\presheaf}}_{\Sigma}(\underline{{{\mathrm{Mot}}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega})
where
\underline{{{\mathrm{Mot}}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}
is the localization of the
G
-category
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}
at the class of universal
K_{G}
-equivalences. The functor
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\simeq\mathrm{Ind}\big((\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}\big)\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G}
induced by the composition
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{loc.}}\underline{{{\mathrm{Mot}}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}\xhookrightarrow{\text{\char 71\relax}}\underline{{{\mathrm{Mot}}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}
is denoted
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}
. There are obvious analogous definitions of absolute/finitary splitting
V
-motives for
V
a finite
G
-set.

Remark 4.2.5
.

By construction and
2.1.23
, these
G
-categories satisfy the expected universal properties which we collect at the end of the subsection.

As before, to construct a
G
-symmetric monoidal category on absolute splitting
G
-motives, it suffices to prove that universal
K
-theory equivalences are stable under norm functors. We do this below after observing the compatibility of our definition of universal
K_{G}
-equivalence with the classical one from
[
BGM+21
]
(thus also justifying the name):

Lemma 4.2.6
.

Let
V
be a finite
G
-set.
A map
{f}\colon\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\to\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
of
V
-stable
V
-categories is a universal
K_{V}
-equivalence if and only if there exists a
{g}\colon\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\to\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
such that

[{g}\circ{f}]=[\mathrm{id}_{\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}}]\in\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})))\quad\text{and}\quad[{f}\circ{g}]=[\mathrm{id}_{\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}}]\in\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))).

Proof.

By
[
Hil26
, Lem. 4.1.12]
, if
E:\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}\to\mathcal{E}
is any
V
-Mackey splitting invariant, the induced map
\pi_{0}\map_{\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\to\pi_{0}\map_{\mathcal{E}}(E(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}),E(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}))
factors through
\pi_{0}\map_{\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\to\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})))\cong K_{0}(\func^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}))
(and similarly for
\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
). Therefore the existence of
{g}
as indicated guarantees that
E({f})
is an equivalence with inverse
E({g})
. This proves that
{f}
is a universal
K_{V}
-equivalence, cf.
4.2.3
.

Conversely, let
{f}
be a Mackey motivic equivalence. Now,
\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},-)))\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}\to\mathrm{Ab}
is a
V
-Mackey splitting invariant, and hence by assumption
{f}
induces an equivalence

\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})))\to\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))).

Picking a preimage of
[\mathrm{id}_{\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}}]
and a lift of that preimage to
\func^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})^{\simeq}
provides a
{g}
with
[{f}\circ{g}]=[\mathrm{id}_{\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}}]
. Now,
\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},-)))\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}\to\mathrm{Ab}
is also a
V
-Mackey splitting invariant, so that

\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})))\to\pi_{0}(K_{V}(\underline{{\func}}_{V}^{\mathrm{ex}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})))

is also an isomorphism. In particular, since
[{g}\circ{f}]
and
[\mathrm{id}_{\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}}]
have the same image under this map, we find that they must be equal. This proves the claim overall.
∎

Corollary 4.2.7
.

Let
w:W\to V
be a map of finite
G
-sets. The functor
w_{\otimes}:\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{W}\to\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{V}
sends universal
K_{W}
-equivalences to universal
K_{V}
-equivalences.

Proof.

Consider the following composite in
\mathrm{Sp}_{V}
, natural in
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{W}
:

(8)

w_{\otimes}\underline{{K}}_{W}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\to\underline{{K}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\to\underline{{K}}_{V}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})).

Here, the first map comes from the lax
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{K}}
, constructed in
3.3.3
, while the second map comes from adjointing over the normed evaluation map
w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\otimes w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\simeq w_{\otimes}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\otimes\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\rightarrow w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
.

The map
Equation

8
is compatible with compositions: since we have a map
(-)^{\simeq}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{K}}}\coloneqq\loops\underline{{K}}
of
G
-lax symmetric monoidal functors
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{S}}}
by
3.3.3
, we get a diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w_{*}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})^{\simeq}\times w_{*}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})^{\simeq}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\loops\Big(w_{\otimes}\underline{{K}}_{W}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}))\otimes w_{\otimes}\underline{{K}}_{W}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{B}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))\Big)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w_{*}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})^{\simeq}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\loops\underline{{K}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\otimes w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\big(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\big)^{\simeq}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\loops\underline{{K}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{W}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},w_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})^{\simeq}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\loops\underline{{K}}_{V}(\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{ex}}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},w_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\circ}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{lax}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{lax}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\circ}

whence the compatibility with compositions. Furthermore, for

, the map
Equation

8
sends the identity to the identity because the composite

To state the main result of this subsection, it will be convenient to use the following notations: let
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
be a
G
-additive
G
-category which admits filtered colimits; we write
\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{split}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}),\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\subseteq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
for the full subcategories of splitting invariants and finitary splitting invariants (i.e. those that additionally preserve filtered colimits), respectively. We also write
\underline{{\func}}^{\times}\subseteq\underline{{\func}}
for the full subcategory of functors preserving finite indexed products.

Corollary 4.2.8
.

The
G
-category
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}_{G}
(resp.
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G}
) is the universal target for absolute (resp. finitary)
G
-splitting invariants. That is, it is
G
-additive (resp. and also
G
-presentable), and for any
G
-additive categories
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
where
\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
is also
G
-cocomplete, the maps

(\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}})^{*}\colon\underline{{\func}}^{\times}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{split}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})

(\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}})^{*}\colon\underline{{\func}}^{L}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{B}}})

are equivalences.

Furthermore, there exists a unique
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}_{G}
(resp.
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G}
) compatible with the norm
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
(resp.
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}
) under the localization
G
-functor
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{abs}}_{G}
(resp.
\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G}
).

Proof.

From
4.2.7
and the fact that the inclusion
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}\subseteq\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
inherits the
G
-symmetric monoidal structure by
C.0.4
in the finitary case, we immediately deduce the symmetric monoidality statement. By the same argument as in the proof of
3.1.13
, using
4.2.3
and that
\mathrm{Ind}^{K}_{H}
preserves filtered colimits and split Karoubi sequences, we see that both the motivic
G
-categories are
G
-semiadditive. That they are furthermore additive may be checked fiberwise and proceeds exactly as in
[
RSW25
, Lem. 6.6]
. Furthermore, the
G
-presentability of
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G}
is also immediate by its construction as a sifted cocompletion.

We are left with showing the first statement about universal properties. We only deal with the finitary case since the other case is similar but easier. Now, we have a fully faithful functor
(\underline{{\mathcal{U}}}_{G}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega})^{*}\colon\underline{{\func}}^{\times}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\hookrightarrow\underline{{\func}}((\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}^{\mathrm{fin}}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
which lands in the full subcategory of splitting invariants since
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}_{G}
was itself a splitting invariant, and
13
13

13

This is the crucial difference with the localizing case.
any split Karoubi sequence is a filtered colimit of split Karoubi sequences between compact
G
-stable
G
-categories by
[
Hil26
, Cor. 4.1.9]
. To see that this is essentially surjective on splitting invariants
(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})^{\omega}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
, simply note that any such splitting invariant will in particular invert the universal
K_{G}
-theory equivalences by definition, and therefore it factors through a functor
\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}_{G}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
which preserves finite indexed (co)products by
2.1.23
. Together with the universal property
\underline{{\func}}^{L}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin}}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}^{\sqcup}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}^{\times}(\underline{{\mathrm{Mot}}}^{\mathrm{split},\mathrm{fin},\omega}_{G},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
of sifted cocompletions by
[
Sha22
, Thm. E]
, this completes the proof.
∎

4.3.
Equivariant THH and the Dennis trace

In this section, we explain how to define equivariant
\mathrm{THH}
, and how to equip it with a
G
-symmetric monoidal structure. This will, in particular, automatically render the Dennis trace
G
-symmetric monoidal as well.

Lemma 4.3.1
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
be a
G
-stable
G
-category. The
G
-presentable
G
-stable
G
-category
\underline{{\mathrm{Ind}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
is dualizable in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
for the tensor product from
[
Hil26
, Prop. 2.2.19]
.

Furthermore, for a
G
-exact functor
\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}
, the induced functor
\underline{{\mathrm{Ind}}}(\mathcal{A})\to\underline{{\mathrm{Ind}}}(\mathcal{B})
is an internal left adjoint, i.e. its right adjoint is
G
-colimit preserving.

Proof.

Indeed, by
B.0.1
and since
\mathrm{Ind}
is fiberwise, it suffices to prove that
\mathrm{Ind}(\mathcal{A}_{G})
is dualizable over
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}
. Since the latter is rigid over
\mathrm{Sp}
in the sense of
[
Ram24
, Def. 4.34]
(see Example 4.40 in
loc. cit.
), we see by
[
Ram24
, Prop. 4.17]
that it suffices to prove that
\mathrm{Ind}(\mathcal{A}_{G})
is dualizable in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
. In turn, this is a classical fact recalled, e.g. in
[
Lur18
, Prop. D.7.2.3]
.

The second part is easy to verify: the left adjoint preserves fiberwise compacts so the right adjoint preserves fiberwise filtered colimits, and it is already
G
-exact.
∎

It follows that the formalism of
[
HSS17
, §2]
provides the following:

to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}}}}_{G}
is a finitary
G
-localizing invariant.

Proof.

That it sends Karoubi sequences to bifiber sequences follows from
[
HSS17
, Thm. 3.4]
, and that it is finitary is standard, see also
[
HSS17
, Cor. 4.25]
.

We now prove
G
-semiadditivity by induction via isotropy separation. So suppose the restriction of
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
to any proper subgroup
K\lneq G
is
K
-semiadditive, and consider, for a proper subgroup
H
and an
H
-stable
H
-category
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
, the canonical map

\mathrm{Ind}_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{H}(\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\to\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}(\mathrm{Ind}_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})

(note that it is sufficient to prove that this map is an equivalence, since
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
is clearly fiberwise semiadditive)

Since restriction to proper subgroups is a strong symmetric monoidal functors, it therefore commutes with symmetric monoidal dimensions, so that for any proper subgroup
K<G
,
\res_{K}^{G}
applied to the above map is a special case of a
K
-semiadditivity comparison map for
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{K}
, which is therefore an equivalence by assumption. Thus, to conclude, we may take geometric fixed points of either side.

For the left hand side, the result is
0
by definition of geometric fixed points and since
H<G
is a proper subgroup, while for the right hand side, it is also
0
: this is because geometric fixed points is also a strong symmetric monoidal functor and hence also commutes with symmetric monoidal dimensions, so that we are left with calculating
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\mathrm{Ind}_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}=0
, which is again true by construction since
H<G
was proper (cf.
2.2.6
and
2.2.7
).
∎

Remark 4.3.4
.

It is not hard to see that
(\mathrm{THH}_{G})^{G}:\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\to\mathrm{Sp}
is not of the form
E((-)^{G})
for any ordinary localizing invariant
E:\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}\to\mathrm{Sp}
. Indeed,
E
can be recovered from
E((-)^{G})
by plugging in induced
G
-stable
G
-categories, so by
G
-semiadditivity of
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
we would have
E({\mathcal{C}})\simeq E((\mathrm{Ind}_{e}^{G}{\mathcal{C}})^{G})\simeq(\mathrm{THH}_{G}(\mathrm{Ind}_{e}^{G}{\mathcal{C}}))^{G}\simeq(\mathrm{Ind}_{e}^{G}\mathrm{THH}({\mathcal{C}}))^{G}\simeq\mathrm{THH}({\mathcal{C}})
, i.e.
E\simeq\mathrm{THH}
.

However,
\mathrm{THH}_{G}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})\simeq\mathbb{S}_{G}
and the
G
-fixed points of the latter satisfies a tom Dieck splitting with terms of the form
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}BW_{G}(H)
. On the other hand, one can show that
\mathrm{THH}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
satisfies a tom Dieck splitting with terms of the form
\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}LBW_{G}(H)
. We explain this for
G=C_{p}
, and refer to the proof of
[
Ram
, Thm. 1.6]
for the general case.

For
G=C_{p}
, we use the isotropy separation localization sequence
\mathrm{Perf}(\mathbb{S}[C_{p}])\to\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}_{C_{p}}\to\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}
to deduce a bifiber sequence of spectra

\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{S}[C_{p}])\to\mathrm{THH}(\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}_{C_{p}})\to\mathrm{THH}(\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}).

This bifiber sequence splits via the unit map
\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}\to\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}_{C_{p}}
, and combining it with the usual formula
\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{S}[G])\simeq\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}LBG
, we obtain the desired formula:

\mathrm{THH}(\mathrm{Sp}^{\omega}_{C_{p}})\simeq\mathbb{S}\oplus\Sigma^{\infty}_{+}LBC_{p}.

Remark 4.3.5
.

Our functor
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
is a reasonable object: when
R
is a connective ring
G
-spectrum,
\pi_{0}^{G}\mathrm{THH}_{G}(R)
is given by the quotient of
\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)
by the commutator
Mackey subfunctor
(as opposed to the levelwise commutator sub-group).

Indeed, combining
[
CCR+25
, Prop. 4.47]
with
B.0.1
we find that
\mathrm{THH}_{G}(R)\simeq R\otimes_{R\otimes R^{\mathrm{op}}}R
in
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}
. Since
R
is connective, we deduce that
\underline{{\pi}}_{0}\mathrm{THH}_{G}(R)\cong\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)\otimes_{\underline{{\pi_{0}}}(R)\otimes\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)^{\mathrm{op}}}\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)
in Mackey functors. The latter is a coequalizer

\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)\otimes\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)\otimes\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)\rightrightarrows\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)\otimes\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)

of the two maps informally described by
x\otimes a\otimes b\otimes y\mapsto bxa\otimes y
, resp.
x\otimes ayb
by definition. From this, the description as
\underline{{\pi}}_{0}(R)
modulo the commutator Mackey subfunctor is clear.

Next, we upgrade the construction of
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
to make it
G
-symmetric monoidal. We again take advantage of the naturality of the construction of
[
HSS17
, §2]
to reduce to one simple claim: that
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
can be viewed as a Mackey functor in (very large)
2
-categories, with emphasis on “
2
” (indeed, in

[
Nar17
, Prop. 3.25]
and
[
HJS
]
, it is already constructed as a
G
-symmetric monoidal
G
-category, i.e. as a Mackey functor in (very large) categories, cf.
[
NS22
, Thm. 2.3.9]
). Since this is a technical point, we have deferred its precise statement and proof to the appendix as
D.0.4
.

Informally, this construction makes the norm functors
\mathrm{N}_{H}^{G}:\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{H,\mathrm{st}}\to\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
into symmetric monoidal
2
-functors. The advantage of this is that this automatically implies their compatibility with symmetric monoidal traces, functorially. This is ultimately what we leverage below:

Corollary 4.3.6
.

The finitary
G
-localizing invariant
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
can be upgraded to a
G
-symmetric monoidal
G
-functor

There are a few versions of equivariant THH in the literature which we expect to be distinct from ours, cf. for instance
[
ABG+18
,
DMP+20
,
CGK25
]
. We close this subsection by highlighting several attractive and naturally desirable formal features of the present construction. For one, it interacts pleasantly with geometric fixed points, as encapsulated by the following:

Proposition 4.3.7
.

There is a natural equivalence of symmetric monoidal functors

\Phi^{G}\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}(-)\simeq\mathrm{THH}(\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}-)\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\longrightarrow\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^{1}}.

Furthermore, for any operad
\mathcal{O}
and
R\in\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathcal{O}\otimes\mathbb{E}_{1}}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
, there is an equivalence

\Phi^{G}\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}(R)\simeq\mathrm{THH}(\Phi^{G}R)

of
\mathcal{O}
-algebras in spectra with
S^{1}
-action.

Proof.

For the first equivalence, we simply note that
\Phi^{G}:\mathrm{Pr}_{G}^{\mathrm{st}}\to\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{st}}
is a morphism of commutative
\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{st}}
-algebras, and hence a symmetric monoidal
2
-functor. Thus, by naturality of traces as constructed in
[
HSS17
, §2]
, we have a commutative diagram in
\cmonoid(\mathrm{Cat})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\mathrm{Pr}_{G}^{\mathrm{st}})^{\mathrm{dual}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{(\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{st}})^{\mathrm{dual}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathrm{Sp}_{G}^{BS^{1}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^{1}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{THH}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi^{G}}

as desired. For the other equivalence, we observe that the functor
\Phi^{G}\colon\mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{LMod}_{\Phi^{G}R}(\mathrm{Sp})
identifies
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
as
\mathrm{LMod}_{\Phi^{G}R}(\mathrm{Sp})
. This is because
\mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
is compactly generated by the set
\{\mathrm{Ind}^{G}_{H}\res^{G}_{H}R\}_{H\leq G}
, and
\Phi^{G}\colon\mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{LMod}_{\Phi^{G}R}(\mathrm{Sp})
is the Bousfield localization which precisely kills the orbits
\{\mathrm{Ind}^{G}_{H}\res^{G}_{H}R\}_{H\lneq G}
and sends the remaining generator
R\in\mathrm{Sp}_{G}
to
\Phi^{G}R\in\mathrm{Sp}
. Hence,
\mathrm{LMod}_{\Phi^{G}R}(\mathrm{Sp})
satisfies the universal property of
\Phi^{\mathcal{P}}\mathrm{LMod}_{R}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
, whence the observation. Combining with the commuting square above, we obtain the second equivalence.
∎

On the geometric side, let us record the following expected result. It further illustrates a certain “regularity” of the
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}_{G}
construction which is not enjoyed by the pointwise THH functor
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\subset\mackey_{G}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{THH}}\mackey_{G}(\mathrm{Sp})=\mathrm{Sp}_{G}
.

.

-colimits. Evaluating at

clearly gives the identity on
\mathbb{S}_{H}
for all

, and so since
\underline{{\mathcal{S}}}_{G}
is generated under

-colimits by the point, we get that
\alpha
is in a natural equivalence, as required.
∎

As illustrations of the foregoing developments, let us record some immediate consequences of all the structures developed thus far.

Example 4.3.11
.

We consider the effect of the equivariant Dennis trace map when the input is the
G
-sphere spectrum
\mathbb{S}_{G}
. Since the trace map is a transformation of
G
-lax symmetric monoidal functors, we in particular have a commuting square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}K(\mathbb{S})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{S})\simeq\mathbb{S}_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{K}}(\mathbb{S}_{G})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}(\mathbb{S}_{G})\simeq\mathbb{S}_{G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

in
\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{G})
, where the identification of the right hand terms with
\mathbb{S}_{G}
is since
\underline{{\mathrm{THH}}}
is a
G
-symmetric monoidal functor. Thus, by applying the symmetric monoidal functor
\Phi^{G}\colon\mathrm{Sp}_{G}\rightarrow\mathrm{Sp}
which satisfies
\Phi^{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}\simeq\mathrm{id}
, we obtain a factorization in
\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp})

K(\mathbb{S})\longrightarrow\Phi^{G}\underline{{K}}(\mathbb{S}_{G})\longrightarrow\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{S})\simeq\mathbb{S}

of the nonequivariant Dennis trace
K(\mathbb{S})\rightarrow\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{S})\simeq\mathbb{S}
.

Example 4.3.12
.

Let
{\mathcal{C}}\in\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
equipped with the trivial
G
-action. By considering the effect of the Dennis trace on
\underline{{\mathrm{Bor}}}({\mathcal{C}})\in\mathrm{CAlg}_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G})
from
Example

2.2.3
and using as above that
\Phi^{G}\mathrm{N}^{G}_{e}\simeq\mathrm{id}
, we get the following diagram in
\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces K({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi^{G}K_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Bor}}}({\mathcal{C}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces K({\mathcal{C}})^{t_{\mathcal{P}}G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{THH}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{THH}(\mathrm{stmod}_{G}^{\mathcal{P}}({\mathcal{C}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{THH}({\mathcal{C}})^{t_{\mathcal{P}}G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{tr}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{tr}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{tr}}

where the horizontal composites are the proper Tate–Frobenius maps (which is the usual Tate–Frobenius map when
G=C_{p}
from
[
NS18
]
),
\mathrm{stmod}_{G}^{\mathcal{P}}({\mathcal{C}})
is the proper stable module category of
{\mathcal{C}}
(cf. for instance
[
HKK24
, Cons. 5.1.2]
. In the case of
G=C_{p}
, this reduces to the stable module category as defined in
[
Kra25
, Def. 4.1]
), and the middle bottom term is by
4.3.7
. The middle vertical map should be viewed as a lift of the proper Tate construction of the Dennis trace map, and we speculate that this diagram might be useful in probing the object
\Phi^{G}K_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Bor}}}({\mathcal{C}}))
, which is an interesting and hard problem related to Swan equivariant K-theory.
