Appendix A
The fixed points–cofree adjunction

In this technical appendix, we work in the general setting of categories parametrized over an atomic orbital category
\mathcal{T}
, in the sense of
[
Nar16
, Def. 4.1]
, with a final object
T
, an example of which is
\mathcal{O}_{G}
. We write
\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}^{\times}
for the nonfull subcategory of
\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}
on those
\mathcal{T}
–categories which admit finite indexed products and morphisms those that preserve these. For
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}
, we write
\int\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
for the cocartesian unstraightening of
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
under the equivalence
\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}\simeq\mathrm{coCart}(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}})
.

Lemma A.0.1
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}^{\times}
. Then the fully faithful inclusion
i\colon{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\hookrightarrow\int\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
admits a right adjoint
R
so that we get a Bousfield colocalization

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i\colon{\mathcal{C}}_{T}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0muR.}

Proof.

Since
T
is final in
\mathcal{T}
, we have a canonical natural transformation of functors on
\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
of the form
\underline{{\operatorname{const}}}_{\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}}{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\to\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
. By the existence of finite indexed products, this is levelwise a left adjoint, and so by (the dual of)
[
Lur17
, Prop. 7.3.2.6]
, the induced functor of coCartesian fibrations
{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\times\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
admits a (relative) right adjoint. Using again that
T
is final in
\mathcal{T}
, the inclusion
{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\times\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
at
T
has a right adjoint, and the composition
{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\times\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
is clearly
i
, so we get the claim by composition of adjoints.
∎

Observation A.0.2
.

Let
{\mathcal{D}}\in\mathrm{Cat}
. Recall from
[
Nar16
, Thm. 2.8]
that there is a 2-adjunction
\int\colon\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{Cat}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0mu\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}
where
\int
is the cocartesian unstraightening. The adjunction counit
\epsilon\colon\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
may be described as follows: precomposing
\epsilon
with the inclusion of the fiber
\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})
of
\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
over
V
, the map
\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\epsilon}{\mathcal{D}}
is given by evaluating at the final object
(V=V)\in\mathcal{T}_{/V}
.

To see this, without loss of generality by restricting if necessary, let
V\colon\ast\rightarrow\mathcal{T}
be the final object. Then the datum of an object in the fiber over
V
of
\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
is equivalent to a map of
\mathcal{T}
–functors
x\colon\underline{{\ast}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
. We now contemplate the commuting square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}),\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}),{\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{\ast}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(\int\underline{{\ast}},{\mathcal{D}})=\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{D}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces V^{*}}

coming from the universal property of the cofree construction. Note here that the bottom equivalence
is
the identification of the
V
-fiber of
\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
as
\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})
. Tracing where the identity in the top left corner goes yields the claim.

Conversely, the adjunction unit
\eta\colon\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
for
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathcal{T}}
may be described concretely as follows: without loss of generality by restricting if necessary, for
V\in\mathcal{T}
the final object, the functor
\eta_{V}\colon{\mathcal{C}}_{V}\rightarrow\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
is given as follows: for
x\in{\mathcal{C}}_{V}
,
\eta_{V}
sends it to the
\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
diagram in
\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
given by sending the unique morphism
w\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
to the cocartesian pushforward
x\rightarrow w^{*}x
. To see this, consider as above the commuting diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{\ast}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}))}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces x^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Tracing where the identity map in the top right corner goes yields the claim because the right vertical
x^{*}
map is precisely implemented by restricting along
x\colon\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}\rightarrow\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
which is a map of cocartesian fibrations over
\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
.

Lemma A.0.3
.

Let
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}_{\mathcal{T}}
and
{\mathcal{D}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}
. Then:

(1)

The
\mathcal{T}
–category
\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
has finite indexed products.

(2)

Under the equivalence
\func(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},{\mathcal{D}})\simeq\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}))
, a functor
F\colon\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
preserves finite indexed products if and only if the associated functor
\overline{F}\colon\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
preserves finite products in each fiber and satisfies the property that for every
w\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
and every
x\in\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\times_{\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}}\{W\}
, the cartesian lift
w_{*}x\rightarrow x
in
\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
is sent to an equivalence by
\overline{F}
.

Proof.

To see (1), for
w\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
, orbitality of
\mathcal{T}
ensures that the right Kan extension
w_{*}\colon\func((\mathcal{T}_{/W})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})
exists because the appropriate limits that need to be taken are all finite products. Moreover, for
u\colon U\rightarrow V
and writing
\sqcup_{i}Z_{i}
for the orbital decomposition of
U\times_{V}W
, the commuting square of restriction functors obtained by applying
\func((-)^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})
to

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\coprod_{i}\mathcal{T}_{/Z_{i}}=\mathcal{T}_{/\sqcup_{i}Z_{i}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{T}_{/U}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{T}_{/W}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{T}_{/V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w}

is horizontally right adjointable by smooth/proper basechange because the map
w
is a cartesian fibration. Therefore,
\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
indeed admits finite indexed products.

For part (2), note first that a
\mathcal{T}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
having finite indexed products is precisely the property that each fiber category has finite products, the cocartesian morphisms of the cocartesian fibration
p\colon\int\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}\rightarrow\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
preserve these finite products, that
p
is in fact also a cartesian fibration, and that these cartesian morphisms satisfy appropriate Beck–Chevalley basechanges. From this perspective, a
\mathcal{T}
–functor
F\colon\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
which preserves finite indexed products is thus equivalently a functor
F\colon\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
over
\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}
which is a map of cocartesian and cartesian fibrations and which fiberwise preserves finite products.

Now, the functor
\overline{F}
is given by the composite
\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\xrightarrow{\int F}\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\epsilon}{\mathcal{D}}
. By
A.0.2
, for
W\in\mathcal{T}
, the restriction of
\overline{F}
to the fiber over
W
is given by
{\mathcal{C}}_{W}\xrightarrow{F_{W}}\func((\mathcal{T}_{/W})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_{W}}{\mathcal{D}}
. In particular, for a morphism
f\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
, the cartesian morphism
w_{*}x\rightarrow x
in
\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
gets sent to
\mathrm{ev}_{V}F_{V}w_{*}x\rightarrow\mathrm{ev}_{W}F_{W}x
. But since for any
d\in\func((\mathcal{T}_{/W})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})
,
\mathrm{ev}_{V}w_{*}d\simeq\mathrm{ev}_{W}d
, we get that
\mathrm{ev}_{W}F_{W}x\simeq\mathrm{ev}_{V}w_{*}F_{W}x
. Under this identification, it is straightforward to check that the map
\mathrm{ev}_{V}F_{V}w_{*}x\rightarrow\mathrm{ev}_{W}F_{W}x
is obtained by applying
\mathrm{ev}_{V}
to the canonical map

(9)

F_{V}w_{*}x\rightarrow w_{*}F_{W}x

coming from the universal property of the cartesian morphism
w_{*}F_{W}x\rightarrow F_{W}x
in
\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
. On the other hand, for any other morphism
u\colon U\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
, recalling the notation from
2.1.8
, we have by the Beck–Chevalley basechange and that
F
was a map of cocartesian fibrations preserving fiberwise products that applying
u^{*}
to
Equation

9
gives the map

(10)

F_{U}(\prod_{i}\overline{w}_{i*}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x)\longrightarrow\prod_{i}\overline{w}_{i*}F_{Z_{i}}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x.

Applying
\mathrm{ev}_{U}
to this map and using the hypothesis that
\overline{F}\colon\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
preserves products in each fiber gives

\prod_{i}\overline{F}\overline{w}_{i*}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x\simeq\prod_{i}\mathrm{ev}_{U}{F}_{U}\overline{w}_{i*}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x\longrightarrow\prod_{i}\mathrm{ev}_{Z_{i}}F_{Z_{i}}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x\simeq\prod_{i}\overline{F}\overline{u}_{i}^{*}x.

All in all, since the evaluation maps
\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
are jointly conservative, we thus see that
Equation

9
is an equivalence for all
w\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
and all
x\in{\mathcal{C}}_{W}
if and only if
\overline{F}u_{*}y\rightarrow\overline{F}y
is an equivalence for all
u\colon U\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
and all
y\in{\mathcal{C}}_{U}
. This completes the proof.
∎

Proposition A.0.4
.

Let
\mathcal{T}
be an atomic orbital category with final object
T
. Then there is an adjunction

\mathrm{ev}_{T}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}_{\mathcal{T}}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0mu\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}
.

For
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}_{\mathcal{T}}
, the unit
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{C}}_{T})
of the adjunction is given at level
V
by
{\mathcal{C}}_{V}\xrightarrow{\eta}\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{C}}_{V})\xrightarrow{v_{*}}\func((\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{C}}_{T})
where
\eta
is the adjunction unit for
\int\dashv\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}
from
A.0.2
, and
v\colon V\rightarrow T
is the unique map. Explicitly, this takes
x\in{\mathcal{C}}_{V}
to the diagram
(\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{C}}_{T}
given by sending
w\colon W\rightarrow V
to
v_{*}w_{*}w^{*}x\in{\mathcal{C}}_{T}
.

For
{\mathcal{D}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}
, the counit
\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
of the adjunction is given by evaluating at the final object
T
.

Proof.

For
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}_{\mathcal{T}}
, we write
i\colon{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\hookrightarrow\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
for the inclusion of the fiber over
T
, which is fully faithful since
T
was the final object in
\mathcal{T}
. Therefore, by the universal property of
\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}
and the Bousfield colocalization from
A.0.1
, we obtain Bousfield colocalization

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func({\mathcal{C}}_{T},{\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},{\mathcal{D}})\simeq\func_{\mathcal{T}}(\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{*}}

Now, by the characterisation from
A.0.3
(2),
i^{*}
restricts to a functor
\func^{\underline{{\times}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},{\mathcal{D}})\rightarrow\func^{\times}({\mathcal{C}}_{T},{\mathcal{D}})
. Conversely, suppose that
\overline{F}_{T}\colon{\mathcal{C}}_{T}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
is a finite product preserving functor. We claim that
R^{*}\overline{F}_{T}=\overline{F}_{T}R\colon\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
corresponds to a finite indexed product preserving functor
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})
. By the characterisation from
A.0.3
(2), it thus suffices to show that
\overline{F}_{T}R
preserves finite products in each fiber and that for each
w\colon W\rightarrow V
in
\mathcal{T}
and each
x\in{\mathcal{C}}_{W}
, the map
\overline{F}_{T}Rw_{*}x\rightarrow\overline{F}_{T}Rx
is an equivalence. But then, writing
v\colon V\rightarrow T
and
f\colon W\rightarrow T
for the unique maps to the final object
T
, we thus have that
f\simeq vw
, and by construction of
R
from
A.0.1
,
Rw_{*}x\simeq v_{*}w_{*}x\simeq f_{*}x
and
Rx\simeq f_{*}x
. It is then straightforward to check that under these identifications, the map of interest is identified with the equivalence
\overline{F}_{T}v_{*}w_{*}x\xrightarrow{\simeq}\overline{F}_{T}f_{*}x
. This proves the claim, so that
R^{*}
restricts to a functor
\func^{\times}({\mathcal{C}}_{T},{\mathcal{D}})\hookrightarrow\func^{\underline{{\times}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},{\mathcal{D}})
.

Therefore, we also have a Bousfield colocalization

(11)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func^{\times}({\mathcal{C}}_{T},{\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func^{\underline{{\times}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},{\mathcal{D}}).}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{*}}

To show that this is an equivalence, it suffices now to argue that for
F\colon\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}
a finite indexed product preserving functor,
R^{*}i^{*}F\simeq FiR\rightarrow F
is an equivalence. Again, by the characterisation
A.0.3
(2) of finite indexed product preserving functors, this is true by hypothesis. By passing this equivalence to groupoid cores, we have thus shown that there is an equivalence

\map_{\times}({\mathcal{C}}_{T},{\mathcal{D}})\simeq\map_{\underline{{\times}}}(\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}}))
which is clearly natural in
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
and
{\mathcal{D}}
. This witnesses the claimed adjunction in the statement.

Finally, to see the descriptions for the adjunction (co)units, simply note that the equivalence
Equation

11
dictates that the adjunction unit and counit are given by

\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\xlongrightarrow{\eta}\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}(\int\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\xlongrightarrow{R}\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{C}}_{T})\quad\quad\quad\quad\func(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathcal{D}})\xhookrightarrow{i}\int\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}({\mathcal{D}})\xlongrightarrow{\epsilon}{\mathcal{D}}

which, together with
A.0.2
, yields the required descriptions.
∎

We can now provide the proof of
2.1.12
, as promised.

Proof of
2.1.12
.

The claimed adjunction is obtained by considering

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}_{G}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{incl}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(-)^{G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\cmonoid}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}}

where the first is by
[
Nar16
, Prop. 5.11]
(see also
[
CHL+25
, Thm. 7.4]
) and the second by
A.0.4
. Now observe that this factors to an adjunction
(-)^{G}\colon\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}_{G}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0mu\underline{{\mackey}}_{G}(-)
via the full subcategory
\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}\subseteq\mathrm{Cat}^{\times}
since for any
G
-semiadditive
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
,
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}^{G}={\mathcal{C}}_{G}
is semiadditive in the ordinary sense. This also uses the fact that
\underline{{\cmonoid}}\circ\underline{{\mathrm{cofree}}}\simeq\underline{{\mackey}}
by
[
Nar16
, 6.6]
or
[
Püt24
, Thm. D]
. The descriptions of the unit and counit are now clear by
A.0.4
.
∎

Appendix B
G
-presentable–stable categories as modules over
G
-spectra

We start with a result of independent interest, which will help us deduce
3.1.13
from
[
RSW25
]
instead of reproving it.

Theorem B.0.1
.

The
G
-fixed points functor
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\rightarrow\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
induces an equivalence of commutative
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
-algebras

\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{G}}(\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}).

Furthermore, a
G
-presentable
G
-stable
G
-category is compactly generated if and only if its image in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
is, and the above equivalence restricts to a symmetric monoidal equivalence

\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{G}^{\omega}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}).

We will use the following lemma:

Lemma B.0.2
.

The
G
-fixed points functor
\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}_{G}\to\mathrm{Cat}^{\oplus}
from
G
-semiadditive
G
-categories to semiadditive
G
-categories is conservative on idempotent-complete categories.

Proof.

Suppose
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\to\underline{{\mathcal{B}}}
is a
G
-semiadditive functor of
G
-semiadditive
G
-categories such that
\mathcal{A}_{G}\to\mathcal{B}_{G}
is an equivalence. In this case, for any subgroup
H\leq G
, by
G
-semiadditivity, the following diagram is vertically left adjointable:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{A}_{G}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{B}_{G}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{A}_{H}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{B}_{H}}.}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\res_{H}^{G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\res_{H}^{G}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{H}}

If
f_{G}
is fully faithful, it follows that
f_{H}
is fully faithful on the image of
\res_{H}^{G}
, and therefore on retracts of objects in the image. But by the double coset formula,
\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{A}_{H}}
is a retract of
\res_{H}^{G}\mathrm{Ind}_{H}^{G}
so that
f_{H}
is fully faithful.

Second, by the commutativity of the above diagram, if
f_{G}
is essentially surjective, then
f_{H}
is essentially surjective on the essential image of
\res_{H}^{G}
. Thus, if
\mathcal{A}_{H}
is idempotent-complete and
f_{H}
is fully faithful, the above retract argument also shows that
f_{H}
is essentially surjective. This proves that on idempotent-complete
G
-semiadditive
G
-categories,
G
-fixed points is conservative.
∎

to0.0pt{\hss\color[rgb]{1,1,1}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{-0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{-0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{-0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.5pt\raisebox{0.0pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{Sp}$}}}}_{G}}(\mathrm{Pr}_{G})
by
[
Hil26
, Prop. 2.2.19]
. By the linear Barr–Beck–Lurie theorem
[
Lur17
, Prop. 4.8.5.8]
, to prove the equivalence, it therefore suffices to prove that the fixed points functor preserves colimits, tensors with objects of
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
, and is conservative. The first two properties are in fact much more general, see
[
MW25
, Prop. 2.4.4.11, Prop. 2.6.3.13]
, and conservativity follows from
B.0.2
.

Now, by definition, an object in
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
is compact if and only if it is so fiberwise, that is, in
\mathcal{A}_{H}
for all
H\leq G
. Since the restriction functors
\res_{H}^{G}
have colimit-preserving right adjoints (the right adjoint is coinduction, which by definition of
G
-semiadditive is equivalent to induction), they preserve compact objects, so an object
x\in\mathcal{A}_{G}
is compact in
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
if and only if it is in
\mathcal{A}_{G}
.

This proves that the equivariant notion of compact is the same as underlying notion in this case, so that compact generation and compact preservation also agree in the equivariant and underlying senses. Thus the equivalence restricts to an equivalence between categories of compactly generated categories and compact-preserving functors on either side, which yields the desired result.
∎

Remark B.0.3
.

The proofs above also clearly works word-for-word when we replace
\mathcal{O}_{G}
with an arbitrary atomic orbital category, in the sense of
[
Nar16
, Def. 4.1]
, with a final object.

Corollary B.0.4
.

Under the equivalence
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{G}^{\omega}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}})
from
B.0.1
, the notion of (finitary) Mackey
G
-localizing invariant and the notion of (finitary)
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}^{\omega}
-localizing invariant from
[
RSW25
, App. B]
are equivalent, and thus the notion of motivic equivalences coincide. In particular, the localization of
\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{perf}}_{G}
at motivic equivalences is presentable stable.

Proof.

On either side, Karoubi sequences are defined as fiber/cofiber sequences, i.e. squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{A}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{B}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 0}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}}

that are both cartesian and cocartesian. Since this and filtered colimits are equivalence-invariants, the notions of finitary localizing invariants clearly agree.
∎

Remark B.0.5
.

The same proof works
verbatim
in the
G
-semiadditive context. In the corollary above, one simply needs to replace
\mathrm{Sp}_{G}^{\omega}
with
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})
and all instances of “
perf
” with
\oplus
’s. But we will not be needing this though.

Appendix C
Finite posets with action and some consequences

Proposition C.0.1
.

Let
G
be a finite group and
\underline{{I}}\in\func(BG,\mathrm{Pos})
be a finite poset with
G
-action. Then
\underline{{I}}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{G}
is a finite
G
-category.

Proof.

We will prove by a double induction on the order of
G
as well as the number of points in the finite poset. The case of
G=e
is standard, so suppose for induction that the statement holds for all groups strictly smaller than
|G|
. We write
I
for the underlying poset, and without loss of generality, it is a connected poset. Suppose we have also shown the statement for a
G
-invariant sieve
{J}\subseteq{I}
.

Now let
x\in I\backslash J
be a minimal element which is not in
J
and write
H\leq G
for its stabilizer subgroup. We need to show that the full subposet
\overline{J}\coloneqq J\cup G\times_{H}\{x\}\in\func(BG,\mathrm{Pos})
of
I
also gives a finite
G
-category
\underline{{\overline{J}}}
. We write
J_{/x}\coloneqq I_{/x}\cap J
for the not necessarily
G
-invariant subposet of
J
.

If
H=G
, then we have
\underline{{\overline{J}}}=\underline{{I}}_{/x}\cup_{\underline{{J}}_{/x}}\underline{{J}}
. Now
\underline{{I}}_{/x}=\underline{{J}}^{\triangleright}_{/x}
is given by
\underline{{J}}_{/x}\times\Delta^{1}/\underline{{J}}_{/x}\times\{1\}
. This is a finite
G
-category because by induction on the number of points in a finite poset,
\underline{{J}}_{/x}
was assumed to be a finite
G
-category already. Hence,
\underline{{\overline{J}}}
is a finite
G
-category in this case.

Next, suppose
H\lneq G
. We may consider the subposet
J_{/x}\subseteq J
as a poset with a
H
–action so that by induction on the order of the group, this induces a finite
H
–category
\underline{{J}}_{/x}
which in turn gives rise to the finite
H
–category
\underline{{I}}_{/x}=\underline{{J}}_{/x}^{\triangleright}
by the same argument as in the previous paragraph.
Then by adjunction, the inclusion
J_{/x}\subseteq{J}
of elements in
J
under
x
induces a map of
G
-categories
G\times_{H}\underline{{J}}_{/x}\rightarrow{\underline{{{J}}}}
. Now we define
\underline{{P}}
to be the following pushout in
\mathrm{Cat}_{G}
and consider the map
\varphi:P\to\underline{{\overline{J}}}
induced by the following commutative diagram:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\times_{H}\underline{{J}}_{/x}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\underline{{{J}}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G\times_{H}\underline{{I}}_{/x}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{P}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\overline{J}}}.}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ulcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varphi}

where the left vertical map is an inclusion of a sieve. In particular,
\underline{{P}}
is a finite
G
-category.

It thus suffices now to show that the map
\underline{{P}}\rightarrow\underline{{\overline{J}}}
is an equivalence.
Since
G\times_{H}\underline{{I}}_{/x}\sqcup\underline{{J}}\rightarrow\underline{{\overline{J}}}
is essentially surjective, so is
\underline{{P}}\rightarrow\underline{{\overline{J}}}
. On the other hand, it is an elementary exercise that there can be no map between elements in the same orbit, and so the composites
G\times_{H}\{x\}\subseteq G\times_{H}\underline{{I}}_{/x}\rightarrow\underline{{P}}
and
G\times_{H}\{x\}\subseteq G\times_{H}\underline{{I}}_{/x}\rightarrow\underline{{\overline{J}}}
are fully faithful (where the former case uses the mapping space formula in
[
HRS25
, Cor. 5.2]
). All in all,
\varphi\colon\underline{{P}}\rightarrow\underline{{\overline{J}}}
is fully faithful when restricted to the full subcategories
G\times_{H}\{x\}
and
\underline{{J}}
. Hence, we are left with showing that for
b\in G\times_{H}\{x\}
and
c\in\underline{{J}}
,
\varphi
induces equivalences

As a consequence of the proof above, we obtain the following:

Lemma C.0.2
.

Let
\underline{{P}}\in\func(BG,\mathrm{Pos})
be a finite poset,
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}
, and
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}\in\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
. Then
\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
and
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})^{\omega}\simeq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\omega})
. Moreover, if
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
is
\omega
–compact, then so is
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
.

Proof.

We prove the first statement about commutation of Ind and compact objects by induction on the size of the poset, with the base of the empty poset being trivial. By the proof of the previous result, we may write
\underline{{P}}
as a pushout in
\func(BG,\mathrm{Pos})

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{M}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{J}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{I}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{P}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h}

where the left vertical map is a sieve inclusion, and by a double induction as in the previous proof, we may assume the desired conclusions on
M,I,
and
J
. We thus have a pullback square

(12)

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{M}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces h^{*}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i^{*}}

either in
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}
or in
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
, depending on whether
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}
is in the former or the latter category.

We claim that in the case when
\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}\in\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
, this is even a pullback
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
. In other words, we will show that
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{X}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
is
\omega
–compactly generated for
\underline{{X}}\in\{\underline{{P}},\underline{{I}},\underline{{J}},\underline{{M}}\}
, that all the maps in
Equation

12
preserve
\omega
–compact objects, and that
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
satisfies the appropriate universal property in
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
. By induction,
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
and
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
are
\omega
–compactly generated by the sets
\underline{{S}}
and
\underline{{T}}
, say. Then
j_{!}\underline{{S}}\cup h_{!}\underline{{T}}\subseteq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
forms a set of
\omega
–compact generators. This is because they form a jointly conservative set since
\mathchoice{\mbox{\uline{\phantom{$\displaystyle\map$}}\hbox to0.0pt{\hss\color[rgb]{1,1,1}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\displaystyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.19133pt\raisebox{-0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\displaystyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{-0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\displaystyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{-0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{-0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.5pt\raisebox{0.0pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{-0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{-0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.5pt\raisebox{0.0pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\map$}}}}(y,h^{*}z)
and
j^{*}\times h^{*}\colon\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\rightarrow\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})\times\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
is conservative, and so we may conclude by
[
Hil26
, Prop. 2.2.14]
. Next, to see that all the maps in
Equation

12
preserve
\omega
–compact objects, we just argue for the case
j^{*}
since the others are similar. For this, the right adjoint is computed as the right Kan extension
j_{*}
. By the pointwise formula, for
p\in\underline{{P}}
, the relevant limit to compute is over the diagram
\underline{{J}}_{/p}\coloneqq\underline{{J}}\times_{\underline{{P}}}\underline{{P}}_{/p}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{G}
. But this is induced by the object
J\times_{P}P_{/p}\in\func(BG,\mathrm{Pos})
, whose underlying poset is finite. Hence, by
C.0.1
, this is a finite
G
-category, so the functor
j_{*}
preserves
G
-colimits and so
j^{*}
preserves
\omega
–compact objects. Finally, since filtered colimits commute with pullbacks, we conclude that an object in
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
is
\omega
–compact if and only if it is so as objects in
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
and
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\underline{{\mathcal{A}}})
under the functors
j^{*}
and
h^{*}
, respectively. From this characterisation, it is clear that the pullback
Equation

12
, which is a priori computed in
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\mathrm{st}}
, is in fact a pullback in
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
.

With this claim established, we now deduce the lemma. By the claim, the equivalence
\mathrm{Ind}\colon\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}\simeq\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}\penalty\mskip 6.0mu plus 1.0mu\mathpunct{}\nonscript\mkern-3.0mu{:}\mskip 2.0mu(-)^{\omega}
, and the induction hypotheses, we get pullback squares

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{M}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})^{\omega}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\omega})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\omega})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{M}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\omega})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lrcorner}

in
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L}_{\omega,\mathrm{st}}
and
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}}
respectively. Hence, we get that
\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
and
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}})^{\omega}\simeq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\omega})
, as required.

Finally, suppose that
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in(\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}^{\mathrm{perf}})^{\omega}
. We will again show that
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
is also
\omega
–compact by induction on the size of
P
again. So suppose we already know the statement for smaller posets, and we write
\underline{{P}}
as a pushout as above. By
[
Hil26
, Prop. 2.5.13]
, we get
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\simeq\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{I}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})\cup_{\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{M}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})}\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{J}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
. Since the right hand side is a pushout of
\omega
–compact objects by the inductive hypothesis, we thus see that
\underline{{\func}}(\underline{{P}},\mathrm{Ind}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}})
is also
\omega
–compact.
∎

Corollary C.0.3
.

Let
\lambda\leq\kappa
be regular cardinals and let
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
be any
G
-presentably
G
-symmetric monoidal category, i.e. an object in
\mathrm{CAlg}_{G}(\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}^{L})
, which is
\lambda
–compactly generated by a set
\underline{{S}}
. Suppose that the set
\underline{{S}}
is closed under the multiplicative norms. Then
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\kappa}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
is closed under the multiplicative norms.

Proof.

First, we note that without loss of generality, we may assume
\lambda=\kappa
. We prove the result by induction on the order of the group
G
, the base case of
G=e
being standard since
S
is closed under tensor products. So suppose we know the statement to be true for all groups of order strictly smaller than
|G|
. By using again the standard consequence that ordinary tensor products preserve
\kappa
–compactness, we are thus reduced to showing that
f_{\otimes}\colon\mathcal{E}_{H}^{\kappa}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}_{G}
lands in
\mathcal{E}_{G}^{\kappa}
for the map
f\colon G/H\rightarrow G/G
, for any
H\leq G
.

Now
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\kappa}
is generated (up to retracts if
\kappa=\omega
) under
\kappa
-small indexed coproducts and pushouts by
\underline{{S}}
, and we note that
\kappa
-small coproducts are
\kappa
-small, filtered colimits of finite indexed coproducts. Thus, we are reduced to showing that the collection of objects of
\res_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\kappa}
whose norm
f_{\otimes}
is
\kappa
-compact is closed under pushouts and indexed coproducts. The proof for both is similar, and easier for indexed coproducts (simply recall that distributivity of the norms implies that norms of a finite indexed coproduct is a finite indexed coproduct of smaller norms) so we do the case of pushouts.

To see this case, let
Y\simeq\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{\Lambda^{2}_{0}}X\simeq X_{1}\cup_{X_{0}}X_{2}
be a pushout where each
X_{i}\in\mathcal{E}_{H}^{\kappa}
is such that
f_{\otimes}X_{i}\in\mathcal{E}_{G}^{\kappa}
. By
G
-distributivity of the
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on
\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
, we thus get

f_{\otimes}Y\simeq\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{f_{*}\Lambda^{2}_{0}}f_{\otimes}X\in\mathcal{E}_{G}.

Note that
f_{\otimes}X\colon f_{*}\Lambda^{2}_{0}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}
is a diagram of
\kappa
-compact objects: at level
G
, since
(f_{*}\Lambda^{2}_{0})^{G}\simeq\Lambda^{2}_{0}
, this diagram is given by
f_{\otimes}X_{1}\leftarrow f_{\otimes}X_{0}\rightarrow f_{\otimes}X_{2}
, which we have assumed to be
\kappa
-compact; at level
K\lneq G
, it is a diagram of terms all of which are indexed coproducts of norms of the
X_{i}
’s, which are
\kappa
-compact by assumption on the
X_{i}
’s and the induction hypothesis (some of the terms are tensor products of norms of restrictions of
X_{i}
’s for smaller groups). Now, by
C.0.1
, since
f_{*}\Lambda^{2}_{0}
is a finite poset with
G
-action, the diagram
f_{\otimes}X
can be re-expressed as an iterated finite colimit of
\kappa
-compact objects, whence
\kappa
-compactness of
f_{\otimes}Y
.

Finally, since this collection of objects is also clearly closed under
\kappa
-small filtered colimits and contains
\res_{H}^{G}\underline{{S}}
, we see that it is the whole of
\res_{H}^{G}\underline{{\mathcal{E}}}^{\kappa}
, as was to be shown.
∎

–compact generators for

,

Appendix D
2-categorical enrichment of norms on presentable categories

We give a 2-categorical upgrade of the
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on the 1-category of
G
-presentable-stable
G
-categories, following the strategy of
[
BB24
, Prop. 2.3.3]
in the nonequivariant situation.

Notation D.0.1
.

We write
\mathrm{CAT}
and
\mathrm{CAT}_{2}
for the (very very large) 1-category of very large 1-categories and very large
2
-categories, respectively. In particular, passing from a 2-category to its underlying 1-category assembles into a product-preserving functor
\mathrm{fgt}\colon\mathrm{CAT}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}
. We also write
\mathbb{C}\mathrm{AT}_{2}
for the (very very large) 2-category of very large
2
-categories. Furthermore, we write
\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}
and
\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}
to denote the 2-categories of large 1-categories and presentable categories, respectively.

Fact D.0.2
.

We collect various facts that we will need to give a 2-categorical enhancement of the
G
-symmetric monoidal structure on presentable-stable categories.

(1)

By
[
BB24
, Prop. A.2.9]
, there is a 2-categorical enhancement of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence
\func(\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G}),\mathrm{CAT}_{2})\simeq\mathrm{coCart}_{2}(\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G}))
, where here a functor
p\colon\mathcal{X}\rightarrow{\mathcal{C}}
with
\mathcal{X}
a 2-category and
{\mathcal{C}}
a 1-category is said to be a 2-cocartesian fibration if for all
x,y,z\in\mathcal{X}
, the square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{X}}(y,z)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\func_{\mathcal{X}}(x,z)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\map_{{\mathcal{C}}}(py,pz)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\map_{{\mathcal{C}}}(px,pz)}

in
\mathrm{Cat}
is a pullback.

(2)

Let
w\colon W\rightarrow V
be a map in
\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
, and
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{W,\mathrm{st}}
. Then by Nardin’s thesis
[
Nar17
]
(cf. the forthcoming work
[
HJS
]
also for a recent treatment which filled in several gaps in the original proof) there exists an object
w_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{V,\mathrm{st}}
and an
w
-distributive
V
-functor
w_{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow w_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
which induces an equivalence

\underline{{\func}}^{\Delta_{w}}_{V}(w_{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}})\xlongrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{{\func}}^{L}_{V}(w_{\otimes}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}},\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}})

for all
\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{V,\mathrm{st}}
. Moreover, these universal distributive functors compose in the following sense: suppose we are given a composition

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces P}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces W}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces U}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces V}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces T}

\lrcorner

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{v}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\bar{w}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces w}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces v}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces g}

of spans in
\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
and
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{U,\mathrm{st}}
. Then writing for instance
\mu_{f,w}\colon w_{*}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow w_{\otimes}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
for the universal distributive functor, the composition

g_{*}v^{*}w_{*}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\xlongrightarrow{g_{*}v^{*}(\mu_{f,w})}g_{*}v^{*}w_{\otimes}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\xlongrightarrow{\mu_{v,g}}g_{\otimes}v^{*}w_{\otimes}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}

agrees with the universal distributive functor
\mu_{f\bar{v},g\bar{w}}\colon g_{*}\bar{w}_{*}\bar{v}^{*}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow g_{\otimes}\bar{w}_{\otimes}\bar{v}^{*}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}
. This is a straightforward check of universal properties using the Beck-Chevalley equivalences
v^{*}w_{*}\simeq\bar{w}_{*}\bar{v}^{*}
and
v^{*}w_{\otimes}\simeq\bar{w}_{\otimes}\bar{v}^{*}
.

Lemma D.0.3
.

The Mackey functor
\underline{{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}}^{\times}\colon\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\to{\mathrm{CAT}}
classifying the cartesian
G
-symmetric monoidal structure upgrades to an object in
\mathrm{CMon}_{G}(\mathrm{CAT}_{2})
, i.e. there exists a finite-product-preserving dashed lift as in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{CAT}_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{CAT}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{fgt}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}}^{\times}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}}

where the vertical map is
D.0.1
.

Proof.

Note that the restriction functoriality clearly has a lift to a 2-functor
\underline{{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}}_{G}\colon\mathrm{Fin}_{G}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbb{C}\mathrm{AT}_{2}
. Using the
2
-category structure of the latter together with the universal property of span
2
-categories, we obtain a unique
2
-functor

\spancategory_{1,5}(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})^{\mathrm{co}}\to\mathbb{C}\mathrm{AT}_{2}

extending the original one, and sending the backwards arrows to the right adjoints of the restriction functors, i.e. to indexed products. Here,
\spancategory_{1,5}
denotes the usual span
2
-category
15
15

15

The subscript
1,5
is meant to evoke that this is a
2
-category, but the
2
-morphisms between spans are themselves only allowed to go in one direction, where there are also span categories where the
2
-morphims are spans between spans.
, also called
2
-category of correspondences in
[
Ste20
, Thm. 1.1.1]
, and we use the universal property established in
loc. cit.
. We may then restrict this functor along the finite-product-preserving functor
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\spancategory_{1,5}(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})^{\mathrm{co}}
to obtain a finite-product-preserving 2-functor
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\mathbb{C}\mathrm{AT}_{2}
. But since
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})
was a 1-category, this factors as a finite-product-preserving 1-functor
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}_{2}
which we denote as
\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}\in\cmonoid_{G}(\mathrm{CAT}_{2})
. Finally, the statement that
\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}
provides the dashed lift is an immediate consequence of the uniqueness of
G
-cartesian symmetric monoidal structures, cf.
[
Ste25a
, Thm. A’]
.
∎

Proposition D.0.4
.

The Mackey functor
\underline{{\mathrm{Pr}}}_{G,\mathrm{st}}^{\otimes}\colon\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\to{\mathrm{CAT}}
classifying the
G
-symmetric monoidal structure upgrades to an object in
\mathrm{CMon}_{G}(\mathrm{CAT}_{2})
, i.e. there exists a finite-product-preserving dashed lift as in the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{CAT}_{2}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{CAT}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{fgt}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{{\mathrm{Pr}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}}

where the vertical map is as in
D.0.1
.

Proof.

The construction, which ultimately goes back to that of Lurie’s
[
Lur17
, §4.8.1]
in the nonequivariant situation, proceeds exactly as in
[
Nar17
, §3.4]
or
[
HJS
]
by replacing all mention of 1-cocartesian fibrations to 2-cocartesian fibrations.

In more detail, by
D.0.2
(1) and
D.0.3
, we obtain a
2
-cocartesian fibration
p\colon\int\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}_{G}\to\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})
. As in
[
BB24
, Prop. 2.3.3]
, we can now consider the locally full subcategory (i.e. the 2-subcategory which induces fully faithful inclusions on the mapping 1-categories)
\int\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\subset\int\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}_{G}
given as follows: an object over a finite set
V\in\mathrm{Fin}_{G}
is given by an object in
\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{V,\mathrm{st}}
; a 1-morphism
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
with
\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{U,\mathrm{st}}
and
\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}\in\mathrm{Pr}^{L}_{V,\mathrm{st}}
lies over a morphism
U\xleftarrow{f}W\xrightarrow{w}V
in
\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})
if and only if the associated morphism
w_{*}f^{*}\underline{{{\mathcal{C}}}}\rightarrow\underline{{{\mathcal{D}}}}
of
V
-categories is
w
-distributive. By construction, it is clear that the underlying 1-category
\mathrm{fgt}(\int\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}})
agrees with the 1-category
\int\underline{{{\mathrm{Pr}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}

Now, by
D.0.2
(2), the restricted functor
\int\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\rightarrow\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})
is a locally 2-cocartesian fibration in the sense of
[
BB24
, Def. A.2.11]
. By
D.0.2
(2) again and
[
BB24
, Lem. A.2.12]
, it is in fact even a 2-cocartesian fibration (note however that the inclusion
\int\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\subset\int\underline{{\widehat{\mathbb{C}\mathrm{at}}}}^{\times}_{G}
does not preserve all cocartesian edges, only the inert ones).

Finally, by performing 2-straightening on this via
D.0.2
(1), we obtain a functor
\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\colon\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}_{2}
which agrees with
\underline{{{\mathrm{Pr}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}
upon postcomposing with
\mathrm{fgt}\colon\mathrm{CAT}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}
. Since
\mathrm{fgt}\colon\mathrm{CAT}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}
reflects products and
\underline{{{\mathrm{Pr}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\colon\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}
is known to preserve finite products already, we also get that
\underline{{{\mathbb{P}\mathrm{r}}}}^{\otimes}_{G,\mathrm{st}}\colon\spancategory(\mathrm{Fin}_{G})\rightarrow\mathrm{CAT}_{2}
preserves finite products. This completes the proof.
∎
